reason: The FAQ answer states Connect is a feature of Transit Gateway that simplifies branch connectivity through native integration of SD-WAN network virtual appliances; claim matches.
The quote lists the same five attachment types as associated to the default route table by default and says you can create additional route tables and associate them.
The quote states cross-account association is possible, only the transit gateway owner can create it, and RAM cannot be used; all three parts match.
The answer under the question about associating a transit gateway with a Direct Connect gateway says you cannot use the same ASN for both.
The quote says VPCs in enforce mode can be connected with VPC Peering or Transit Gateway to guarantee end-to-end encryption; claim matches.
The quote carries both parts, including the 'without exclusions' condition and the ability to connect VPCs in different Encryption Controls modes.
Read with its question heading on gradually migrating VPCs to encryption, the quote says TGW supports incremental migration by handling encrypted and unencrypted traffic.
The quote states enabling encryption on an existing TGW is non-disruptive and attachments migrate to encrypted lanes seamlessly and automatically.
The claim is framed as what that FAQ answer states; the quoted sentence under that question heading says all VPCs must be in the same region.
The quote names VPC Peering or Transit Gateway and says encryption support must be turned on explicitly using console or modify-transit-gateway.
The quote says yes and that traffic stays encrypted from the source until the TGW attachment in the destination VPC regardless of its encryption status.
The quote states no routing between VPCs with identical CIDRs and that the new VPC route is not propagated into the TGW route table.
The quote says limits are in the documentation and to create a support case to exceed them, but it does not say they are not in the FAQ; that clause is the author's inference.
The quote states multicast within and between VPC attachments and not over Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN and peering attachments.
The quote states the transit gateway will have a default route table and that multiple route tables are optional.
The quote defines Network Manager as a Transit Gateway feature that centralizes management and monitoring of networking resources and branch connections.
The quote says TGW routes are not propagated to the VPC route table and the VPC owner needs to create a static route.
The quote says that when you connect VPN or Direct Connect Gateway, routes propagate with the on-premises router using BGP.
The quote states peering attachments do not support route propagation and static routes are needed in TGW route tables.
The quote says routes decide next hop from destination IP and lists the same five target types.
The quote describes segmenting with multiple route tables associated with VPCs and VPNs, creating isolated networks similar to VRFs.
The quote states dynamic and static routing between attached VPCs and VPNs; claim matches word for word.
The quote states VPC CIDR propagates on attach or resize into the TGW route table using internal APIs, not BGP.

The quotes support the source-owner default and the destination and TGW owner options, but the November 21, 2025 date appears only in the page's posted-on line and the link of those options to a metering policy stands only in the surrounding text.
The announcement quote states there is no additional charge for using FCA on Transit Gateway.
The quote states Flow Logs capture IP traffic to and from transit gateways and publish to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose.
On the Transit Gateway Flow Logs page the quote says flow log data is collected outside the traffic path and does not affect throughput or latency.
The two best-practice quotes state no extra transit gateways for HA because they are HA by design, and a single transit gateway per Region for redundancy and DR.
The quote states hub and spoke for VPCs and on-premises, fully managed, no third-party appliances to provision and no VPN overlay required.
The quote says Direct Connect plus Transit Gateway using transit VIF attachment to a Direct Connect gateway connects several regional centralized routers over a private dedicated connection.

Under the Transit Gateway + Site-to-Site VPN heading the quote describes an AWS-managed VPN endpoint for multiple VPCs in the same region without the cost and management of multiple IPsec connections.
The quote states return to the TGW in the same AZ after Network Firewall inspection, enabled by appliance mode, which also gives stateful inspection in the security VPC.
The quote advises being selective about traffic through Network Firewall or GWLB to reduce costs, for example by inspecting between untrusted zones.
The two quotes on the GWLB with Transit Gateway page say appliance mode should be enabled for east-west inspection and is enabled to ensure flow symmetry because GWLB endpoints are a routable target.
The quote states the default AZ-affinity behaviour and the cross-zone behaviour across all registered and healthy targets in enabled zones.
The quote recommends separate inspection VPCs in local Regions to avoid inter-Region dependencies and data transfer costs, inspecting locally.
Under the isolated VPCs with shared services heading the quote says attachments can route to and receive from shared services, for isolated groups using a shared service.
Under the Isolated VPCs overview the quote says inter-VPC packets route through the TGW and are blocked because there is no route in its route table.
Under the Isolated VPCs heading the quote says each isolated router has a single route table and attachments of one router cannot reach another router's attachments.
The quote says create one network ACL for all subnets associated with the transit gateway and keep it open inbound and outbound.
The quote matches the claim: limit the number of TGW route tables unless the design requires multiple.
Under the Metering policies heading the quote says you can specify a maximum of 10 middlebox attachments.
The quote states a policy can contain up to 50 entries evaluated from lowest to highest rule number.
The quote states each transit gateway can have only one metering policy.
The metric table row defines BytesIn as bytes received by the transit gateway with Sum as the only meaningful statistic.
The table row defines PacketDropCountBlackhole as packets dropped for matching a blackhole route, statistic Sum.
The table row defines PacketDropCountNoRoute as packets dropped for not matching a route, statistic Sum.
The quote states the transit gateway enforces MSS clamping for all packets.
The quote states an MTU of 8500 bytes for traffic between VPCs, Direct Connect, Connect and the three kinds of peering attachments.
The quote states the MTU mismatch risk when migrating from VPC peering and the advice to update both VPCs at the same time.
On the Transit Gateway quotas MTU section the quote says traffic over VPN connections can have an MTU of 1500 bytes.
On the Multicast in AWS Transit Gateway page the quote states support for IGMPv2 and both IGMP and static group membership domains.
The quote states multicast routing between subnets of attached VPCs and that the TGW acts as a multicast router.
The quote states that with instances and the TGW association in the same subnet, the same network ACL applies in both directions.
The quote states a Network Firewall attachment is created with appliance mode automatically enabled, eliminating explicit management of inspection VPCs.
The quote states a network function attachment connects the TGW directly to Network Firewall and eliminates creating and managing inspection VPCs.
The two quotes from the same Note under the Network Firewall integration heading state static routing only on Network Firewall attachments and that third-party firewalls are not supported.
The whitepaper quote advises placing the TGW in the Network Services account for centralized management and sharing it with RAM across Organization accounts in the same Region.

The quote says 'the subnets in this VPC'; that 'this VPC' is the Network Firewall security VPC stands only in the preceding text, which also says that VPC has a separate subnet per AZ for the TGW attachment, so the 'only endpoints' scope is not carried by the quote alone.
The quote states both halves: no default route table when both are disabled, one is created when either is enabled.
The quote states transit gateways do not support PMTUD on Site-to-Site VPN, Direct Connect and peering attachments.
The quote states no DNS resolution for custom DNS names of attached VPCs set up with Route 53 private hosted zones.
The quote covers identical and overlapping CIDRs and that the new VPC routes are not propagated.
The quote states typically one TGW per Region with route tables for isolation, and a valid case for multiple gateways for blast radius, control plane separation and administrative ease.
The quote states a transit gateway cannot have more than one VPC attachment to the same VPC.
The quote states PBR is available at no additional charge beyond standard transit gateway fees.
The quote states a policy table replaces the route table on an attachment and an attachment has either one, not both.
The quote states the peer owner must accept the request and a static route pointing to the peering attachment is added.
The quote states inter-Region peering uses VPC peering infrastructure, AES-256 at the virtual layer between Regions and at the physical layer outside AWS control, hence double encrypted there.
The quote states intra- and inter-Region peering with IPv4 and IPv6 traffic and a peer in your or another account.
The whitepaper quote states peering in the same or multiple Regions on the same infrastructure as VPC peering and therefore encrypted.
The quote states 'In general, the transit gateway has a sender pays model'; the claim keeps the 'in general' hedge.
The quote states only static routes are supported for transit gateway peering attachments.
The quote states PMTUD support for traffic ingressing on VPC and Connect attachments.
The quote states the TGW owner is billed hourly for Connect attachments (SD-WAN appliances).
The quote states data processing per GB sent from a VPC, Direct Connect, VPN or Network Firewall to the TGW, with 1 GB = 1024 MB.

The quote supports the default allocation to the source attachment owner, but the fact's adjustable condition (flexible cost allocation can customize it) stands only in the next sentence, not in the quote.
The quote states the Direct Connect Gateway owner is billed hourly for Direct Connect attachments.
The quote states charges for connections made to the TGW per hour and for traffic flowing through it.

The quote gives $0.04 = $0.02 processing on TGW #1 + $0.02 outbound inter-Region transfer, but the scenario (1 GB sent over a peering attachment from N. Virginia to Oregon) is only in the preceding sentence, and the claim drops the 1 GB volume the amounts depend on.
